decisions.executionNote: Use left arm for the left basket; lift and progressively orient downward with small continuous elbow-up motions.
Approach above the rear egg in the left basket, maintaining clearance while rotating to a near-vertical grasp.
Align the left gripper vertically over the rear egg, then inspect before final descent.
Refine rear-egg alignment from the wrist view and descend gradually with the gripper open.
Rear egg is centered between the fingers; close gradually while lowering slightly, then inspect retention.
Lift the closed gripper clear of the basket and check that the rear egg moves with it.
The egg remained in the basket. Reopen, align over its shifted position, and descend lower for a better grasp.
Adjust toward the rear egg in the wrist view and narrow the fingers during a slow final descent.
The egg shifted toward the robot rather than lifting. Reopen, raise slightly, and recenter over its new position.
Close around the centered egg without further horizontal contact, then perform a short vertical retention test.
The egg slipped toward the front. Reposition farther toward the robot so the egg lies deeper between the jaws before closing.
Center the front-left egg laterally between the open fingers, close at fixed height, and test a short lift.
Continue the closed-gripper lift and inspect whether the centered egg is retained above the basket.
No egg retained. Reapproach the front-left egg with open jaws, lowering to a deeper grasp rather than pinching its top.
Adjust the grasp toward the front egg's center and close at the deeper height; use a small lift to test retention.
Lift vertically with the gripper closed; verify the front egg stays between the fingers as the basket recedes.
The egg is visibly retained. Carry it inward above the basket rim toward the holder, keeping the gripper closed.
Carry the retained egg toward the holder's left rear cup, staying above the rim before final alignment.
Lower the retained egg toward the rear-left cup while refining its lateral alignment; do not release until close to the holder.
Tilt the left wrist inward while retracting slightly left to maintain egg alignment and ease the final descent into the rear-left cup.
Correct the egg leftward and slightly forward over the rear-left cup, release gently, and raise to inspect placement.
First egg is released in the rear-left cup. Withdraw toward the basket and restore a near-vertical pickup orientation.
Approach the front egg remaining in the basket with open fingers and a nearly vertical wrist.
Replan from the observed wrist pose after tracking lag; approach the front egg slowly and restore the downward grasp orientation.
Lift away from the basket rim before shifting left to center the front egg; avoid forcing the observed tracking obstruction.
Withdraw substantially upward to clear the rim and remove the persistent lateral tracking obstruction before retrying the pickup.
With the rim cleared, restore the successful near-vertical orientation and descend over the front egg with slightly narrowed open jaws.
Fine-align slightly right and forward while descending to the deeper grasp height for the front egg.
Close around the centered front egg without pushing farther against the rim, then lift slowly to verify retention.
The front egg slipped out. Reopen, shift toward its center, and lower to a deeper grasp before closing again.
The egg rolled away from the front rim. Move forward to recenter it deeper between the jaws before closing.
Close on the centered egg at the deeper height, then lift vertically to check retention.
Lift the apparently retained second egg clear of the basket, keeping the gripper closed and beginning a gentle inward carry.
Carry the retained second egg toward the front-left cup, tilting inward slightly to keep the wrist on the left side.
Align the second egg over the front-left cup and descend gradually while retaining it.
The second egg slipped onto the table in front of the holder. Withdraw the left arm and prepare the right arm to recover it without crossing arms.
Move the left arm clear above its basket and approach the fallen egg with the right arm from its own side, rotating downward gradually.
Bring the right gripper above the fallen egg with an open, nearly vertical grasp; hold the left arm clear.
Fine-align the right gripper with the fallen egg and lower around it, keeping the fingers open.
Center the fallen egg deeper between the right fingers, close, and test a short vertical lift.
Lift the recovered egg with the right gripper closed and verify retention before moving it over an empty cup.
Move the recovered egg over the front-right cup with its grasp orientation unchanged to reduce slipping.
Seat the recovered egg farther into the front-right cup, then open the right gripper without changing orientation.
Withdraw the open right gripper to verify seating, while aligning the left arm above the remaining left-side basket egg.
Two eggs are visibly seated. Clear the right arm outward and descend the left gripper toward the left remaining egg.
Fine-center the third egg between the left fingers, close without dragging, and test a short lift.
The third egg slipped toward the robot. Reopen and approach its shifted center from farther back at a deeper grasp height.
Close around the centered third egg at the deeper height, then lift vertically without changing orientation.
Lift the visibly retained third egg clear of the basket and begin carrying inward without rotating the grasp.
Carry the third egg toward the front-left cup at constant height and orientation, with the grasp kept closed.
Continue toward the front-left cup with unchanged grasp orientation; slow descent while the egg remains visibly retained.
Fine-align the third egg with the front-left cup and lower it close to the holder bottom before releasing.
Release the third egg in the front-left cup, then withdraw the open gripper to verify seating.
Three eggs are visibly seated. Return the left gripper above the basket to collect the final egg, keeping the right arm clear.
Approach above the final egg with the same stable grasp orientation, leaving room for wrist-view alignment.
Refine alignment over the last egg, narrowing the open jaws slightly to avoid the basket rim while descending.
Clear the obstructing basket rim, shift left above the egg, and straighten the wrist for a vertical approach.
Descend vertically over the last egg with the jaws open, now clear of the basket rim.
Fine-center the last egg farther between the jaws and descend to the deeper grasp height.
Recenter slightly left around the last egg, close at the current depth, then test a vertical lift without rotating.
Lift the last egg clear of the basket with the grasp closed and unchanged, checking retention before transfer.
Carry the last egg inward at safe height, adding a small gradual inward tilt while keeping the left wrist on its own side.
Bring the last egg over the rear-right cup using an inward tilt while keeping the left wrist left of center and the right arm clear.
Lower the last egg toward the rear-right cup with the grasp orientation fixed, using the head view because the lid occludes the wrist view.
Avoid further pressure against the lid. Shift the egg left and forward over the rear-right cup, then release and inspect.
All four eggs are released in the holder. Clear the left gripper from the lid and prepare the right gripper for a gentle closing push.
The last egg appears perched between the right cups. Clear the left arm and inspect it closely with the right gripper before closing the lid.
Approach the perched fourth egg with the right gripper open, aiming to reseat it in the empty rear-right cup.
The lid occludes the right wrist view. Recenter backward over the perched egg using the head view, keeping the jaws open.
Back away from the lid obstruction and reorient the right gripper for an angled approach from its own side.
